items.stem: What causes day and night on Earth?
options: The Earth rotating on its axis once every 24 hours
items.answer: The Earth rotating on its axis once every 24 hours
items.markingKey: Rotation (spin) about the axis; orbit takes a year.

items.stem: Explain why it is summer in the Southern Hemisphere when it is winter in the Northern Hemisphere.
items.answer: The tilt of the axis means the Southern Hemisphere is tilted towards the Sun at that time: longer days and more direct sunlight, while the north is tilted away.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: tilt; 1 mark: angle/day length effect.

items.stem: Explain why the Moon always shows the same face to the Earth.
items.answer: It rotates on its axis in the same time it takes to orbit the Earth (about 27 days).

items.stem: Explain why the length of daylight in Oslo, which is at a high northern latitude, varies the way it does through the year.
items.answer: Near the equator day length stays about 12 h all year; at high latitudes it varies greatly (long summer days, short winter days), because the tilt changes how much of each latitude circle is lit.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: tilt of axis; 1 mark: correct pattern for that location.

items.stem: Explain why the length of daylight in Reykjavik, which is near the Arctic Circle, varies the way it does through the year.

items.stem: Jupiter orbits the Sun at an average distance of 7.78 × 10¹¹ m with a period of 4333 Earth days. The gravitational field strength at its surface is 24.8 N/kg. (a) Explain why planets further from the Sun have longer orbital periods. (b) Calculate the time for light to travel from the Sun to Jupiter.
items.answer: (a) They travel a longer distance per orbit and move more slowly because the Sun’s gravitational field is weaker there. (b) 2590 s

items.stem: How long does the Earth take to orbit the Sun?
items.answer: About 365 days

items.stem: Explain why we see the Moon even though it does not produce light.
items.answer: It reflects light from the Sun towards the Earth.

items.stem: Explain why a lunar eclipse can only happen at full moon.
items.answer: Only at full moon is the Earth between the Sun and Moon, so its shadow can fall on the Moon.

items.stem: Explain why the Sun appears to move across the sky from east to west.
items.answer: The Earth rotates from west to east on its axis.

items.stem: Which list shows planets in order from the Sun?
items.answer: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter

items.stem: Explain why the inner planets are rocky while the outer planets are gas giants.
items.answer: Near the young Sun it was too hot for volatile substances to condense, so only rock and metal formed planets; further out, gases and ices could gather into giant planets.

items.stem: Explain why a comet’s speed changes during its elliptical orbit.
items.answer: Close to the Sun the gravitational pull is stronger and it gains kinetic energy as it falls in; it slows as it moves away.

items.stem: Data for some planets (distance from Sun / million km; orbital period / Earth years; surface temperature / °C): Mercury 58, 0.24, 167; Venus 108, 0.62, 464; Earth 150, 1.0, 15; Mars 228, 1.9, −65; Jupiter 778, 11.9, −110. items.answer: (a) Period increases with distance, faster than in proportion. (b) Venus has a very thick CO₂ atmosphere giving a strong greenhouse effect. (c) About 29 years (Saturn); extrapolating the pattern is uncertain because the relationship is not linear.
